findings.summary: Sealed unit tests take expected register values from the generated LL macros; register-definition faults are invisible to them (r101 0/6, r102 1/6 killed) while the RM-derived oracle kills 6/6 each.
inspection/regmap.py generate() and check_regmap() both use rm_registers()/parse_section(); a parser defect would be common-cause. No defect resulted here (independent parser agrees 48/48).

Mutant count<timeout -> count<=timeout (r102 hal_rcc.c:21, would allow 1001 polls vs SWR-015) survives sealed tests; killed by access-counting oracle IT-013/014. Sealed code itself complies (polls == timeout).

On timeout the HAL clears HSION even when HSI was already ON before the call (RM0486 reset value HSION=1); SWR-013 says 'clear the enable bit it set' and the code comment says 'this call set'. Requirement/implementation ambiguity for reviewer disposition (OBS-001).
unit_verification_summary metrics passed=1/executables=1 count test binaries, not the 51/26 executed checks.

usage-by-agent.json reports basis unknown ('no Fabro run id'); the package cannot show author/inspector model diversity. Launch record: all roles ran deepseek-flash (correlated-AI verification threat).

LL uses read-modify-write on RCC_CR/AHB1ENR/AHB1RSTR (rw per RM, legal) although RM0486 provides atomic set/clear registers (14.10.128 RCC_CSR, 14.10.185 RCC_CCR, 14.10.147/204 AHB1ENSR/ENCR); interrupt-concurrency hazard if called from multiple contexts (queued CAPA SWE3-03).
Sealed host tests reset the register array to 0, not the RM reset values (RCC_CR=0x00000008), so reset-state behaviour (F-04) is not exercised.
